ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: What happens to fish if pelicans increase?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the right side of the figure is an “Aquatic food chain (aquatic food chain)” aquatic food chain, labeled from bottom to top as Phytoplankton (phytoplankton), Zoo-plankton (zooplankton), Fish (fish), Pelican (pelican), and the arrows point from the lower organisms to the upper organisms, including from Fish to Pelican. Reasoning: In a food chain, arrows indicate that energy flows from the one being eaten to the predator, so Pelican eats Fish. If pelicans increase, the predation pressure on fish will increase, therefore the number of fish will decrease.
